notes.title: Version 1.020 update
notes.notes: [p]A new update to the game after over a month of release. This update is a small head start to the major update that is to come sometime in the future. As I continue to progress with online match play and further improvements to the game, I wanted to provide some quick fixes to some issues I have noticed and wanted to addressed. Here are the following changes.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]v1.020[/b][/p][p][/p][h3]Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]Daiyousei no longer reverts to default color if using her desperation in alternate color.[/p][/*][*][p]Nitori no longer enters opponent's side when using a bomb.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Campaign[/h3][list][*][p]Set starting points to 10.[/p][/*][*][p]When picking Marisa, you no longer play as Reimu during the first match against Sakuya + Remilia.[/p][/*][*][p]Opponent wagers can now go up to 9.[/p][/*][*][p]Loser's bracket now only requires you to defeat 3 opponents.[/p][/*][*][p]During the final boss, projectile power up now adds to the reserves.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Gameplay[/h3][list][*][p]Lily now delivers ball to the left side in tutorial rather than center.[/p][/*][*][p]Shop prices lowered by around 20 - 30 percent from previous version's price.[/p][/*][*][p]Gem values have been increased with some having a value of 10 up to a maximum of 50.[/p][/*][*][p]When you have less than 15 points, opponents are much easier.[/p][/*][*][p]Upper spike has been altered when on top of the screen. Now your ball will actually go down instead.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Character Stats[/h3][list][*][p]Yuugi's upper spike has been decreased.[/p][/*][*][p]Youmu's desperation now has a taller hitbox.[/p][/*][*][p]Youmu's Bomb black out graphic has been slowed down.[/p][/*][*][p]Youmu's fully charged blade can now split into smaller blades when ball touches it.[/p][/*][*][p]Nitori's bomb now has variables to it. You must now collect opponent projectiles in order to get the maximum amount of bubbles to disperse.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]General[/h3][list][*][p]Added new color palettes. Access the third color by pressing the bomb button in character select.[/p][/*][*][p]Smaller micro updates and typo fixes.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I also want to go over into detail a few of these changes.[/p][p][/p][p][i][b]Opponent wagers can now go up to 9[/b][/i][/p][p]During the campaign, every once in a while, you may get a challenge that is worth more than a single point. Originally, this only went up to 5, with the higher number being more uncommon. To alleviate the grind of having to reach 100 points, I have now increased the wagers up to 9. The higher numbers are still uncommon, but you should now be able to get higher wagers.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/0fd4dd08c10dc1fef333b7180110322fafc60a56.png"][/img][/p][p][i][b]Loser's bracket now only requires you to defeat 3 opponents[/b][/i][/p][p]Before, you had to climb out of loser's bracket with -10 points. This turned out to be a challenge for most players, and they sunk deeper into negative points. This has been altered to only give you -3 points and any loses leads to an immediate game over. But your progressed is saved, so now you only need to defeat 3 opponents before restarting the tournament with 10 points.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/f36e90a6712b7c61aea99bf7879cc0e43398487d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][i][b]Upper spike has been altered when on top of the screen. Now your ball will actually go down instead[/b][/i][/p][p]There was an oversight where some characters could go to the top of the screen, use the upper spike to bypass the opponent and hit the wall. This lead to easy victories as the opponent could not do anything. This was perfectly displayed by Yuugi who could get the ball to a very high altitude with a high speed and she having the highest power stat would lead to easy victories every time. This has been addressed by having a normal spike no longer elevate, and high spikes actually now drop the ball. Interesting note about this, I was originally going to implement this early on in the game's development, but I never got around to actually adding it and simply thought it was not necessary. I wasn't anticipating the issue, but perhaps in the back of my mind, this was perhaps the reason why I thought of this in the first place. But this is still a new concept to add to the game and will surely change how it plays, so do leave a comment on what you think of this new implementation.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/12f382de881282193ef1291be1dc4dad90b7a495.png"][/img][/p][p][i][b]Added new color palettes. Access the third color by pressing the bomb button in character select.[/b][/i][/p][p]Self explanatory, but I wanted to make a note of it since it may not be so obvious. In a future update of the game, I will add a separate menu to select a color palette rather than have button presses. Also here's a little tip. Select Random and press either the projectile or bomb button. Now you can preview the alternative color without having to select the character first.[/p]

notes.title: Status on upcoming online and new updates
notes.notes: [p]I wanted to give you guys a quick update on how things have been going since the launch of the game, especially with the announcement of online implementation about a month ago. I will also go over future plans for the upcoming Version 1.100.[/p][p][/p][h2]Status of online matchmaking[/h2][p][/p][p]To summarize the progress of online, it is going great. Much has been done to progress this mode, including testing the online from one state to another. The results were very satisfactory. Issues are present and I am working on dealing with these issues, but I can confidently say that online can be implemented into the game around next month. It's going to take that long because this stage of getting the game online is just the first of two stages. This first stage is setting up the online infrastructure for the game. The objective of this first stage is to simply get a connection between to game sessions. Here's how it works using screenshots of the current online alpha:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/e202c478e4cdc5929ab988439ee95b931f4bc5cb.png"][/img][/p][p]The idea behind online for Touhou Volleyball Danmaku is that a player hosts a lobby and 2 or 4 players can join in.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/cafd4b729642a39d8fe342d0164bdded42c1e3c0.png"][/img][/p][p]Once the game detects that all players are ready, you will be sent to the lobby where you can chat. At this time, you are assigned predetermined position but the complete version will allow you to select which position you wish to be in.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/bd384d9af1831416c487d2ca85e462033ddfb376.png"][/img][/p][p]And then you enter the game proper. Though at this time, I haven't actually tested the actual game online, just using some test dummies who can only move. And this actually works. I managed to make the characters move on two machines, both locally and from another state. I am confident enough that this system can work on the actual game, I just need to look at a few issues before I proceed to stage 2.[/p][p]Stage 2 is translating the gameplay tomake it viable to function on a network as directly as it does locally. What that jargon means is to make sure every little thing actually behaves the way it should over the internet. Here's how it technically works. When a player makes a server, they are the ones handling all the data going in and out, including from the player they are playing as. All other players are simply sending their data so the host can distribute it to everyone. So the host is handling everything: the players positions, when and which button a player is pressing, the ball's position, the UI, every little projectile that comes out, everything is being handled by the host to makes sure that their data reflects that on the other player's screen.[/p][p]I'm willing to give it a shot and make sure every character's specials and shots are one to one in the game, but if it becomes too difficult to actually do so for a particular type of projectile or special move, I'm going to have to make some changes to some characters special moves. While projectiles, bombs, and desperation of any design are no real problem on a local game, going online presents the challenge in that creating a projectile requires a lot of configuration that the host needs to process. A simple projectile has data for their position in the screen, how fast they are going, what angle their trajectory is, etc. This all has to be processed by the game in real-time and if some of the special moves become too cumbersome, then changes will have to be made to that special move both online and locally. But if such changes were to happen, then perhaps now is a good time as there will be a big update for the game coming to version 1.100.[/p][p][/p][h2]Version 1.100 changes[/h2][p][/p][p]After weeks of the game being out and spending time making micro updates, I got around to watching other players time with the game as well as playing it myself. I haven't had a chance to simply play my game, which I manage to do for a few days. I thank everyone who has been patient with the game but for sure, from what I have experienced, changes need to be done. I am planning on balancing the characters, making needed changes to the difficulty curve of the campaign, and add more modes to the game that I didn't have time before the launch. While I'm still planning these out, I will give a brief bullet point on what I am planning doing for the release of Version 1.100[/p][p][/p][p]* Fix/replace the dynamic difficult of the story campaign[/p][p]* Decrease the prices of the store and have sales more frequent[/p][p]* Make point distribution more abundant[/p][p]* Add arcade mode[/p][p]* Make the events challenges in campaign available on the main menu[/p][p]* Include a character information screen on the main menu to learn how the play[/p][p][/p][p]While many players managed to get through the campaign just fine, I feel that it is unbalanced for others, particularly those who did not play the demo, which I admit never came to mind. I didn't figure people would buy the game before trying it, but if that is the case, I will be putting consideration for those players.[/p][p]And a quick note for those who sign up for a custom fairy, I will be working on that as the final task for version 1.100. I haven't forgotten about your fairies, but you will have to wait a bit longer before they appear in the game.[/p][p][/p][h2]Quick update and online beta[/h2][p][/p][p]Before version 1.100 is released, I will be releasing another smaller update. This smaller update will fix some of the issues I listed above, mainly those that can be implemented easily. I will also be uploading a beta branch which will contain an online test version that will be tested with a few characters. As I said earlier, online will require extensive planning to account for all the players special moves, so I'll probably be using the first four characters, Reimu, Marisa, Sakuya, and Remilia for this beta to test out how to implement online for all characters.[/p][p][/p][p]That is all I have to report. Thanks for your patience and support. The game's development continues.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: A week later. What else is in store for the game?
notes.notes: [p]The launch week has passed and it's been quite a week for myself. I spent all this time doing fixes, adding things, taking suggestions, and implementing features. It was quite a week that still continues. But I wanted to take a break from updating the game to lay out my thoughts about what the future holds for the game. As I mentioned, this game is intended to be constantly updating, and I don't mean just these micro-updates. What I wanted to do was add more substantial updates to prolong the life of this first version before moving on to version 2, which will be like a completely different game. But I'm getting ahead of myself as I still have version 1 to deal with.[/p][p]So what is version 1 about? To put it simply, v1 is suppose to be the base game, the foundation of future updates. We're setting up the basic structure for future additions. So I want to take a moment and list out what I have planned for version 1[/p][p][/p][h2]Online mode[/h2][p][/p][p]We're starting off big. I was thinking that online was going to be reserved for v2, but I changed my mind when I started playing my own game. That's right, Only recently had I a chance to play my own game, not for fixes but for fun. During the week, after spending the day doing fixes, I would play my game for my own enjoyment. I guess it sounds ridiculous coming from me but I had a lot of fun playing my own game. I did end up wanting to change a few things, which I managed to do in some of the updates, but there was on update that I could not update but really wanted: online. While I was having fun with the campaign, I really wanted to go online and play with my fans and I figured that you guys probably feel the same way. That's why I'm announcing it right now, online is the first priority for v1. I won't be waiting for v2, and in fact, perhaps this is for the best. To get a head start on online would serve me well in the long run as I can keep it updated to prepare for v2's many new features.[/p][p]I'm going to start planning out how online could work so this feature won't be coming anytime soon. I just wanted to let you know that online is now my next priority because this game can't wait to get that feature, it needs it now.[/p][p][/p][h2]Mini-games and arcade mode[/h2][p][/p][p]Throughout the game campaign, there are various challenges that will pop out. These are some of the mini-games you can play but I didn't had a chance to actually make a menu for them, but I didn't have time to do that. There is also one or two more mini-games I wanted to add but didn't have time for that either. But eventually I'll make time to make a menu and add any new challenges I wanted to add.[/p][p]But one feature I do want to make is an arcade mode. This is nothing more than a just going against every single team, just like an ordinary arcade game. This idea came about when I played some games that have an arcade like experience but no actual arcade mode. I would've loved to just go against the opponents one after another until the end. That is why I feel it is important to add this feature, because an arcade like game needs an arcade mode. And there may be a special surprise waiting for you.[/p][p][/p][h2]Thank you Fairy[/h2][p][/p][p]The slots for the special community event, the Thank You Fairy, have all been filled up so quickly. I was kind of surprised there was such a demand for what can amount to a mere sticker in the end credits. But then again, I'm sure you're going to be really surprised with what I have planned. So I thank everyone who has made a request and if you missed out on this, there will be plenty of opportunities in the future to get another fairy. For now, I gotta figure out a method of making this happen, because I got to set time to get all your requests made. So be patient as you won't be getting the instructions just yet.[/p][p]--[/p][p]That is all I have to report. I am still accepting suggestions, reports, feedback, and anything else you guys want in the game. The experience has been great updating and improving the game and it couldn't happen without you guys. So keep on playing, keep the suggestions coming, and let's make this the best Touhou fangame ever (a man can dream).[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The release of the game, what comes next, and Thank You Fairies
notes.notes: [p]I feel like I've been saying this a lot but, it's finally come down to this. The game has officially been released. After two years of working to get this game off the ground, I managed to finally get the base game ready. This doesn't mean the game is complete because the vision I have for the game is bigger than the time I had to reach this point. But if I didn't release the game now, the game would never be released due to the scope. That is why I wanted to offer a base game and build upon it over time, and that's what's happening right now.[/p][p]What the base game has to offer is the campaign mode where you can play as any of the characters to get one of 7 endings. Each ending is based on the pairings on the character select screen vertically (i.e. Reimu and Marisa, Sakuya and Remilia, etc.) You can just play as one of these two characters to receive an ending. But aside from the story, there are some side attractions that will keep you busy for some time, such as weather events and challenges. The other addition to the base game is more options for the versus mode. You can now select how many match points to reach, wall health, even if you want power ups or not. So now you can play with your friends in custom matches.[/p][p]But as I mentioned, this game is continuously being built. While we're still a bit away from version 2, there are some things that I want to add to version 1. But they are small things, mainly having to do with music. I left music as the last task as that is my weakest talent, but there wasn't much time in the end to add many new songs. But if gameplay is what really matters, then that aspect should do you well. There are a few things that need some fixing and adding, but pretty much the game should be solid, I just want to add some extra things to improve the game. And there are plans for more modes in the next update as well such as an arcade mode and the mini games and challenges available outside the story campaign.[/p][p]And finally, I wanted to give thanks to the Touhou community for making this happen, and I wanted to have a bit of fun while I'm at it. This is an idea I got as I was brainstorming with my brother and that is Thank You Fairies. To show my appreciation to you guys who have helped me get this far, I'm going to offer you guys a personal fairy in the game. Where they will appear is not certain yet as I'm still planning this, but you can be sure that I will have a fairy with your name on it, or whatever message you want to send.[/p][p]There will be more details about this later but for now, if you want a future update to contain a fairy with your name or some personal message, then the first 100 people who purchased the game and makes a request will get a custom fairy. There will be a thread on the Steam forums with more information about this.[/p][p]Thank you so much guys. This has been quite an adventure, one that continues moving forward. Let's make this the best Touhou fangame ever.[/p]

notes.title: The Second Demo is now available
notes.notes:
The long awaited second demo has arrived. This has been a long time coming because this isn't just another demo. It's what the final game will more or less look like. There's going to be plenty of changes in the coming weeks for sure but there are some things you should know.

One is a major announcement in itself but I'll give you a brief rundown here. Around next month, perhaps by the end of June or early July, will be the release of the full version. This game has been in development for nearly two years, but considering the scope of this game, I'm going to need more time to see its completion. As I mentioned many times before, this "full" version is actually more like the base game. It's going to have enough features to keep you entertain, but there's still more to come later down the line. All these future features will be free updates so you guys just need to buy the base game and you will get everything down the line eventually for free afterward. More information on that when the time comes.

For now, the second demo is here to showcase the possibilities of what this full-fledge game can be. But I must admit that this demo was rushed by the end of it. I wanted to release this demo to coincide with the announcement on the YT channel which was today, but that only gave me a week to work with and it wasn't enough time. There are still some things I didn't get to add like some sound effects for some attacks, and there are even some issues that I've discovered in the end that I will be fixing in the coming weeks. But time is not on my side, so any fixes that I make will have to coincide with the development of the base game. There's still so much to do but little time left, so I'm going to have to do some fixing on this new demo in the next few days. After that period, I'll be developing for the base game exclusively.

I won't go into details about what changes will be made or what needs to be fixed, but I will mention that if you have played the teaser demo and load up this new version of the demo, you may not be able to move in the main menu. That is because I didn't have time to optimize the save file. The base game is going to have a new save file because it's apparent that I need a specific save file for the base game. So it's best if you simply delete the old save file and start fresh. There is no menu option to do this, but there is a workaround.

When you boot up the game, hold down F11 when the loading screen appears. If you get the option to select a language, that is the sign that the file has been successfully deleted and the game should work like normal.

And that is about it. Enjoy the new demo and tell me what you think about on the Steam forums. I'll be going through any new threads to see what issues you have, any suggestions you give, or just general comments you have about the game.

notes.title: Introducing Ran and Chen
notes.notes:
We now conclude this series of spotlights with the final team, Team Shinigami. Please note that all gameplay shown on the gifs are still a work in progress and are subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/6f5afaf1943d8356a7a82ed3744d6654dd3fc61b.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Good control of the ball and capable of entering the opponent's field
[b]Con[/b]: The longest meter out of any character with the highest cost

She was sent by Yukari to investigate the latest incident, but she can't help but have a little fun while she's at it. With her computational abilities, she has impressive control of the ball. You may find that each type of ball hit may suit a particularly need more so than any other character. Her movements are more or less average, so her best approach with the ball is to practice knowing what type of hit to use in what situation. On the side of abilities, she has powerful attacks that can overwhelm the opponent due to the sheer amount of projectiles she can produce. But this comes at a cost, a great cost. Just like in our current economy, the costs are outrageously inflated. Both her projectile and desperation meter are the longest of any character with their activation having equally high cost. You will be grazing and collecting ammunition for a long while before you can actually use any of her attacks. But the price may be worth the cost as you may end up with a very powerful character if you know when to use them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/14ddf2deea4b169d3d84925513becfd7cfd03b04.gif[/img]

Her projectile has her summon a tiny star, but as the star slowly travels to the opponent's side, it will grow in size. If it touches anything other than the ball, or if you press the projectile button again, it will explode into smaller stars. The bigger it gets, the more stars that are shot out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/e54d653891d79385b368baaa76e65aea4d184aab.gif[/img]

Her bomb causes all of the opponent's projectiles to be drawn to her. Once the bomb button is pressed, Ran will collect all of the opponent's projectiles, causing them to hover around her. After a while, all of the collected projectiles convert into projectiles of her own. During this state, you can cross over into the opponent's side as she continues to pollinate the field with her projectiles. Once she exhausted her supply, she returns to her side of the field.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/56f6052bb46bdb81d9168bc98e4eceab63371087.gif[/img]

Her desperation has her spin really fast, and in this state, tap the desperation button to shoot out a barrage of projectiles. This in itself may not be much as the spinning does not protect you from projectiles, and while the desperation meter drains slowly, shooting your projectiles takes a considerable amount of the meter. But if you managed to save up your projectile and bomb, you can overwhelm the opponent with so many projectiles on screen, you'll be forcing the opponent to play in lunatic difficulty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/daea9f2ebc5aeaf3aea9ea3931a64d105d6cb08e.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Great speed with capability of entering the opponent's field
[b]Con[/b]: Abilities may feel like they lack something extra

The little shinigami whose more than excited to play some volleyball. What cat doesn't love chasing a ball and Chen is no exception. She has very quick movements and while her hitting power isn't all that impressive, it is by no means lacking. Utilize her speed more so than hitting the ball and you should find Chen to be a very good character to use. The use of her abilities, on the other hand, may not be impress most players. They are still good and you may find uses for them in strategy, but they may feel "off" if you are used to the ways other characters use their abilities. But despite these shortcomings, there may be secrets waiting to be uncovered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/895d2f43dd7c033d9d7522a8848a7b9a4bb06789.gif[/img]

Her projectile has her spinning around and spreading her projectiles in a spiral pattern. A beautiful display of danmaku but perhaps it would be more appropriate in a actual bullet-hell as it may seem as a waste to some players. Could there be a way to utilize all of her bullets to attack the opponent?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/447cffa91108c1a3778d7b37a8d44efbd7b10cef.gif[/img]

Her bomb also has her spinning but this time she collects bullets. But while every other character has the bullets automatically affected or attract the opponent's bullets, Chen has to gather the bullets manually. If the entire field is full of the opponent's projectiles, it should be no problem for you but not for your partner as they will still have to dodge any bullets coming their way. Be sure to not use this bomb to help your partner unless you are close to them to collect the bullets. After a short time passes, Chen will convert all collected projectiles into her own and shoot them at the opponent. The more you collect, the more projectiles will be shot out. If none are collected, she will merely shoot out a small burst. And if you want to shoot your projectiles early, simply tap the bomb button again to unleash whatever you have collected.

Her desperation allows her to enter the opponent's field. Once you activate her desperation, she will naturally being to spin and will be able to intercept the opponent's field. Be aware that her movements have decreased to a crawl, and her dash in contrast are incredible fast, maybe too fast as you may find it uncontrollable. But in turn you may enter the opponent's field to mess around, keep them from having control of the ball, and perhaps any other type mischief you can discover.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/4c4fb9796e6d4ba8b19feb9c05fa3d2e4d85f5ea.gif[/img]

And that is all of the characters. May these announcements help you in the upcoming second demo and the future full version. There are further plans after the game is released, and no doubt future characters will make an appearance, so this won't be the end of the roster reveals. For now, come back to  these announcements when the second demo is released.

notes.title: Introducing Yuugi and Suika
notes.notes:
The roster is nearing completion as we move on to the next team, Team Oni. Please note that all gameplay shown on the gifs are still a work in progress and are subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/ef668d7750d7dc52704a8d74ab0de32148a50077.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: The strongest character in terms of hitting power with a devastating abilities to match.
[b]Con[/b]: Very slow and has a heavy feeling to her movements.

There is no other youkai who exemplifies power than an oni, and Yuugi is the best example of such. You may be fooled at first as her serves seem to be relatively average, and her movements are quite slow. But its when she spikes the ball when you see her brutal strength. The ball goes soaring like a cannonball, and doing just as much damage to the opponent's wall. It only takes a few hits to shatter their wall and with its incredible speed, the opponent may be tempted to remain near the wall like a goalie. This is when you trick them by utilizing her average serves and lobby the ball at the very center of the field. You'll have the opponent scramble to the front of their field to save the ball, in which you can then destroy them with a burst of projectile. Yuugi truly is a real monster when you know when to use her abilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/0aedd22967c3f49d902222e15e37a61ea513f637.gif[/img]

Her projectile is a burst of danmaku. Much like a shot gun, she will blow a great amount of danmaku in a short and quick burst. And we mean it when we say quick and short as it disappears just as quickly as it appeared, giving it a very short range compared to every other character's projectile. This attack is best use when the opponent is close to the center. If the opponent plays it safe and keeps their distance, some of the danmaku from this burst does travel a longer distance, but it it is slow and uncontrollable. It's best to use this as intended and wait for the opponent to get close to her range.

Her bomb is a powerful shockwave that shakes the screen and destroys all of the opponent's projectiles. The shock can even stop the ball in its tracks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/c1ab4aca4f7bd3c99d3de64dce65d06a84230004.gif[/img]

Her desperation has her turn around and shatter her own wall. With a powerful punch, Yuugi will destroy her wall in order to create shards. Depending on how much health the wall had, you can have up to a thousand shards flying through the playing field, which the opponent will have to deal with on top of any other obstacle they are facing already. Needless to say, this is a risk as it leaves your side of the field open for an easy point. Note that this move does not transfer towards the next rally as all shards, regardless of whether they are on-screen or not, will be removed when a rally ends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/0f7e4547ee12493b3b743c27c3071720b3e9298f.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Strong hits with many options of control.
[b]Con[/b]: Awkward movement.

The oni who is always drunk thanks to her never-ending gourd, except that it has gone missing, causing her to be sober for the first time in centuries! But perhaps its this sobriety that she now has a clear head and can actually focus on a game of volleyball. And this focus will pay off in using Suika's skills and abilities. Being an oni, she has very powerful hits on the ball. Whether you spike, pass, or serve, all her hits are strong and powerful. Each type of hit on the ball has its own use, so if you want to give the opponent some panic, spike the ball for a hard hit, or give it high bounce when you need time to think as it will remain in the air for some time. Her abilities are no slouch either when she uses her mist ability. All of these skills could make her a contender for best character had it not been for the very strange movements she possesses. She has been drunk for so long, she has taken her drunken movements to muscle memory. She is slippery, her dashes are more like nudges, and she has trouble slowing down. It will require a real zen master to figure out how to manage her unorthodox movements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/738037afebfa3a059eb65d79747fe24ce7abed00.gif[/img]

Her projectile has her hurl a boulder at her opponent, but don't think this is merely throwing a rock. Hold down the button and you will see a chart. This chart shows you how far the boulder will travel. Hold down the ball button and you can increase the altitude. Release the projectile button and send the boulder flying to the parameters you have given it. Even if it misses your target, simply tap the projectile button once more and the boulder will shatter into pieces, flying in all directions. A great and versatile projectile that can be more effective when you learn how to control it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/6d9a8e53863ec3fc7b9aaf44945731b9c1a6c378.gif[/img]

Her bomb allows her to turn her opponent's projectiles into mist. Just a good ol' basic bomb.

Her desperation has her cover her entire side of the field into mist. And from this mist, smaller versions of herself will start popping out, aiming to ram into the opponent. As long as you have meter, the mist will remain in place, even in-between rallies (but the mini-Suika's won't pop out during this time). The mist can even protect you by destroy all of the opponent's projectiles, making it a perfect shield. You may also hit the desperation button again and all the mist will transform into a huge plethora of items.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/c45b46d34ff67b4e52bf1577f0fa959d23fff09f.gif[/img]

Stay tuned for the next announcement as we will spotlight the final team of the roster.

notes.title: Introducing Aya and Nitori
notes.notes:
We'll be looking at the next team in this series of introductions, the Youkai team. Please note that all gameplay shown on the gifs are still a work in progress and are subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/209a0456db470935be02f2288346b077077a2fa7.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Incredible speed with powerful abilities.
[b]Con[/b]: Most abilities do not provide benefit to the player.

You practically already know the game plan of the fastest tengu in Gensokyo. But Aya is not just about speed, but also about control. Being the fastest character, she can dash across the playing field in a blink of an eye, and with little inertia, she can stop at the drop of a pin. In other words, Aya was designed to not just be fast but effective with that speed. But still, some players may find her a bit slippery at first so practice would be best to get the hang of controlling her. But her speed doesn't just apply to her movement. While her stats may not be out of the ordinary, she emphasizes in covering distance when it comes to hitting the ball. This does not mean her hits are the strongest, but merely that she aims to keep the ball traveling for as long as possible. Aya is all about getting things done quick but also in a controlled manner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/4adcd6624014bbc14320f7673ad903eaea50979a.gif[/img]

Her projectile is a wind blade that allows her to control its trajectory. Tapping the projectile button while holding still will shoot the blade forward, but if you are moving up or down the blade will incline slightly in the direction you are moving. Holding down the projectile button while moving up and down will increase this incline. It will awkward at first but once you get the hang of it, you can use this to target an opponent no matter where they are on the screen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/78db5a0b183a2c0917146414a247235f8a2650d4.gif[/img]

Her bomb makes use of her fan that will blow away everything on the screen. Projectiles, items, the ball itself, and even the opponents will be affected by the fan. But unlike the bombs of every other character, her bomb does not make a distinction between player or opponent. That means that every item and projectile, whether friend or foe, will be blown away. Take caution with this bomb as if there is an item on your side of the screen, it too will be blown away.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/343895c990f8d3ee654ce2e019e6d76eea265087.gif[/img]

Her desperation has her summon a small tornado. It isn't strong enough to pull in the players or the ball, but any projectile and item that appears on screen will be sucked into its vortex. But much like the bomb, it will not distinguish between projectile and item. This is another ability where you must be sure that you are willing to pay the cost of not utilizing your projectiles and giving up all items on your side of the screen for a short period of time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/2a64087a61a351244de44fbd8b49edcaf2221394.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Abilities can overwhelm the opponent due to their sheer amount
[b]Con[/b]: Sluggish and clunky movements

The kappa with a bag full of tricks, or she would be if she didn't lose it. But even without her large backpack, Nitori can still put up a great defense as her abilities can dish out a great number of projectiles to annoy the opponent. She doesn't have the best movements as she feels sluggish and heavy, and her stats are more on the average side. But what she makes up for these lacking features is her abilities to keep the opponent at bay. You can use her projectile to enclose the opponent, her bomb to surprise them with a big hit, or her desperation to make them claustrophobic. Nitori is a case where her offense is her best defense.

Her projectile is an undulating stream of bubbles. Nitori can shoot out a stream of bubbles that are close to each other to create a chain. This can be used to enclose the opponent, and their undulating nature makes it difficult to graze. This is truly one projectile that will hit the opponent's nerves.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/a708851a87d5653915fbf8f77221205f5aa6cd43.gif[/img]

Her bomb is a shield that protects her from all incoming projectiles. When the shield is activated, a bubble will surround her that will absorb every projectile that it hits. But there is a limit to how many projectiles it can take, and if it goes over capacity, it will explode into a burst of its own projectiles. You can even activate this attack earlier than expected by pressing the bomb button again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/9f951efe88fbfaac87d97ba0e573c577642777e7.gif[/img]

Her desperation has her summon a wall of bubbles. Upon pressing the desperation button, giant bubbles will rise from the bottom and slowly advance toward the opponent's field. These bubbles are quite dense as it will take a number of projectiles to pop a single one, let alone all of them, with the exception of strong attacks such as bombs. The ball itself can interact with the bubbles as the ball is powerful enough to destroy each one, but the bubbles will also cause the ball to bounce off. If the ball is on your field when summoning this wall, the bubbles will push it off, and it may end up coming back down, destroying bubbles as it bounces around. That is why its best to summon the bubble wall when the ball is on the opponent's side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/9ea4f864cf3db1914df58d5d74aa4f8aa3079838.gif[/img]

The series continues next time.

notes.title: Introducing Youmu and Alice
notes.notes:
We now continue this small series with the introduction of the Puppet Team. Please note that all gameplay shown on the gifs are still a work in progress and are subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/a7caef599cb07638cf277dd0ccda8b8814171ce4.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Good hitting power and strong abilities.
[b]Con[/b]: May be too meticulous and slow-playing for most players.

The diligent yet meek gardener, Youmu makes her appearance but you probably already saw her appearance coming. But one may find Youmu in this game to be quite technical in her approach to volleyball. The best way to describe her is "straightforward". Perhaps literally as her movements are much more linear than any other character and her hitting power leans more towards horizontal directions. She is also a character that requires patience to use due to her abilities. Youmu is recommended for more advance players.

Her projectile is a charge attack. Hold down the button and you will see you projectile meter be consumed. Let go of the button to unleash your attack. The longer you charge, the wider the attack becomes. Do note that you cannot move during charging. You can still be hit by a projectile but you won't lose your concentration. The ball on the other hand will break your concentration, which will cause Youmu to lose concentration. Be aware of this as you will not regain you projectile meter should it happen, but you can keep the ball from interrupting you with the help of her ghost half, which you will be able to control as long as you are charging.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/5da3cdf0f8a09696c75d0b714ac541452fe569a6.gif[/img]

For her bomb, when the opponent has their projectiles on the screen, the screen will turn black as she targets all of the opponent's bullets and slices each one in half. A quick and simple bomb with a pretty cool effect.

Her desperation may be the hardest one in the game to utilize. When you have a full meter and press the desperation button, Youmu will stand in place, concentrating on what is in front of her. You won't be able to move around in this state, but just like her projectile, her ghost-half can be controlled. While In this state, what you are waiting for is to get your "target" in Youmu's line of sight. When you believe that your "target" is within her sights, tap the Desperation button again and the screen turns black as a line streaks through the screen. Suddenly everything stops as Youmu returns to her spot. Once back where she was, anything in her line of sight will be damaged. The "target" I was mentioning could be anything on the screen, from the player itself who will lose a life, to the ball that will be sent flying across the screen at a high velocity. And even if you didn't hit anything, you will at least give the wall pretty good damage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/b0d99dfeb37e57b3c54db2cbcc39b2d2ddee866d.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/0cdd6003c522185be00de68b4a3d42e9dab96b5e.png[/img]

[b]Pro[/b]: Has the opportunity to overwhelm opponent with a barrage of projectiles.
[b]Con[/b]: Average stats when it comes to hitting the ball.

Gensokyo's puppet master comes to play some volleyball, and she's not alone. Alice brings her dolls along for backup as her abilities make use of them extensively. She leaves the offensive tasks to her dolls which can shoot projectiles or explode into shrapnel. Perhaps this is to make up for her not too impressive stats. They're not the worse as her movements are pretty decent and has some good hitting power. One can say they are just average at best but when you start playing as her, you will soon learn that she was meant to utilize her dolls.

Her projectile has her place a doll on the screen which will target a player and shoot at them continuously. You can place up to 5 dolls on the screen. At the rate they shoot, that many dolls will surely give the opponent a workout in dodging, but for every shot taken by each doll means consumption of your meter. Too many dolls on the screen and you will see you projectile meter drop dramatically.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/5106081b9000b715489b19813a072a2a7589dd21.gif[/img]

Her bomb has her summon 8 dolls who will hover on the screen. Whenever an opponent's projectile is detected on your side of the field, the closest doll will rush to absorb it. No matter how many bullets there are, the dolls will seek each and every one. But there is a limit to how many they can take. If they absorb too many, they will explode dispersing projectiles. This explosion can also be activated by pressing the bomb button again, or if the doll remains on the screen for too long without absorbing any bullets. And the best part is that they are not regulated to their side of the field as they can freely move to the opponent's side.

Her desperation has her summoning a giant doll. She will serve as a shield, absorbing all bullets, and you can make her shoot a pattern of projectiles by the press of the desperation button. The doll can even stop the ball if it hits her. But be aware the desperation meter. Merely being in the field drains it slowly, but every bullet she absorbs, every projectile she shoots, and even the ball hitting her, will cost meter.

[u]_________________________________________[/u]

We're nearly halfway there. Tune in to the next announcement as we continue to reveal the rest of the roster.

notes.title: Introducing Cirno and Daiyousei
notes.notes:
Now we are moving on to the rest of the cast, being showcased for the first time, starting with the Fairy Team. Please note that all gameplay shown on the gifs are still a work in progress and are subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/b1d3b778bf18119b53822cc411f41e3744293173.png[/img]

[b]Pro[/b]: Quick movements and a great horizontal hitting power.
[b]Con[/b]: Lackluster projectile and bomb.

No introduction is needed for here you have the strongest volleyball player, or so she would like you to believe. With Cirno's fast speed and pretty good hitting power, perhaps she does have a case. However, what she won't tell you is her vertical hitting power. While she has a very good horizontal (Orange, Red) when hitting the ball, her vertical (Blue, Green) is on the extreme side as it literally flies upward nearly 90 degrees. Good to pass to the partner above you but not much else. Her projectiles are also nothing special, but she makes up for it by having pretty good bombs and desperation. She's all about utilizing her strengths and completely ignoring her weaknesses.

Her projectiles consists of her shooting three large icicles with two moving at opposing angles. Hit the projectile button again and each will shatter into three smaller icicles that are slightly faster. While this may seem like a good gimmick to have, it may prove difficult to actually control. When you shoot out the icicles, you have to press the projectile button again to shatter them, meaning that your output of projectiles are delayed due to needing to press the projectile button twice to shoot another round. The smaller projectiles also do not spread out, following the same trajectory as the large icicle they spawned from. This makes it easy to predict where the bullets will head towards. And to add to this, her projectile meter is very small. You will fill it up quickly and this means you don't have much ammunition to work with. This is truly a difficult projectile to utilize, but it doesn't make it impossible to come up with clever ways to trap your opponent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/49a95f16c3f4ce9141433b400a93b897c5e5e19a.gif[/img]

Her bomb freezes every one of the opponent's projectiles and after a second, they will explode into shards of smaller icicles to injure the opponent. But the trajectory of these smaller bullets are still predictable. The best use of her bomb is when the screen is full of the opponents bullets to create a wall of icicles coming towards them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/1046a3b4c5f8a81eb4ba2131168628dba9ac74e6.gif[/img]

Cirno's desperation allows her to curse the ball with a freeze spell. When you activate her desperation, the ball will turn blue. When the next opponent touches the ball, the curse will transfer to them and they in turn will turn blue. In this state, they cannot use their projectiles, bombs, or desperation. They also can't collect items of any kind, including health and bombs. Their meters are literally frozen in place for a set amount of time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/0cd8e3f028c661d2bdc5746e543b763e030b2cc2.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/5a3c98f18d8ea9923e047ed94ae6d5fccff87ecf.png[/img]

[b]Pro[/b]: Large projectile meter gives her more ammunition and access to her desperation whenever she has any meter.
[b]Con[/b]: Seriously lacking in offense.

The timid Daiyousei, wanting show off her volleyball skills, or maybe she was forced to play when her pal insisted that she joined. She may not be the strongest like her friend, especially since she prioritizes on self-preservation, she can still provide good defense with her swift speed. She also has a very good vertical, but perhaps she has taken this to the extreme as even her horizontals tend to have a more vertical arc. And this may be her demise as her strongest hit on the ball will seriously be lacking. If you insists on having her pass the ball, make sure it's near the center of the field, otherwise you will risk having the ball flop towards the ground. But despite these shortcomings, Dai-chan does have her advantages.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/58ecc8be77590211da9565cb73ea89dcb98d1dd7.gif[/img]

Her projectile has her shooting 5 yellow orbs that will spread out the further they go. Because of her generously long meter, she can shoot out a barrage if you allow it to fill up. And to add to her arsenal, if you hold down the projectile button on the last shot, every one of her bullets on-screen will home-in on the closest opponent they detect.

Her bomb allows her to disappear and reappear right in front of the ball. When the ball is moving towards your field, hit the bomb button and she will immediately teleport to intercept it every time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/643df00b10331015c065d054944e7e3d0960d6d7.gif[/img]

Her desperation is a special case. When activated it, she will become transparent and no projectile can hit her, but she can still interact with the ball. But not only can you activate and deactivate her desperation anytime you want, you do not have to wait till the meter is filled up. Unlike every other character, as long as she has any amount of desperation, she can use this power anytime she wishes. And while the meter itself is rather small, there is a generous amount where you will probably never be without this power. But do not be too careless as it also drains rather quickly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/901c61b12fab428d89a7ce1b6b2eb1be09e673d5.gif[/img]

Be sure to tune in next time for the next team highlight.

notes.title: Introducing Sakuya and Remilia
notes.notes:
The gamplay details of the Scarlet Devil team. Please note that all gameplay shown on the gifs are still a work in progress and are subject to change.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/0f096692ff19ab3542e9c7aa0f9d3548991c8e88.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Very quick movements with exceptional meters
[b]Con[/b]: Not very strong when hitting the ball

Efficient in serving the ball as she serves her master, Sakuya is about getting to her task quickly. Her quick movement allows her to dash across the field to reach the ball no matter what, but it comes at the price of her hitting power. You will find her ability to hit the ball lacking, Which is probably the reason why she makes up for it with her projectiles and abilities. It is recommended to play her as backup more than anything.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/a4aa0d96ef4b1c7f320ac0aafbcf7cfa95ca835a.gif[/img]

Her projectiles are her ever trusting knives. She will fling 9 knives spread out to cover a wide area. Though they move slowly, she can dispense a great cluster of knives thanks to her generous projectile meter. Quick to fill with each shot at a decent cost, you will never run out of knives with her.

And as if flinging a barrage of knives wasn't enough, she has also brought her time-manipulation powers. When the opponent has her cornered with their projectiles, she can use her bomb which stop time and allows her to replace each of the opponent's projectile with two knives of her own. That means more of the enemies projectiles equals two times the trouble for them. And when her desperation meter is filled, she can activate a slow down that will cause everything to decelerate, causing everything to go in slow-motion. All you have to do is tap the desperation button to turn on or off this power but be aware that keeping it on drains your desperation meter. As long as she has meter, she can do this as much as she wants. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/4102973f8aad4a38a0083c292ad982e8d037b7d4.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/e2b56d2a4a57876335d01e93719382b7381793fb.png[/img]
[b]Pro[/b]: Excellent speed with a very strong hit to the ball.
[b]Con[/b]: Long meters for both Projectile and Desperation forces player to rationalize when to use them.

The ever bored vampire makes her appearance to play some volleyball. And being a vampire, Remilia won't hesitate to use her natural vampiric abilities. She is not only one of the fastest in the roster but also one of the strongest. A good spike will send the ball flying and crashing onto the opponent's wall, crushing a large chunk of its health. Her speed is also top notch as she can traverse the screen in a blink of an eye. But all this power comes at the price of very long meters with output that may have much to be desired compared to other characters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/83e3e2eef2ee912f5e730997fc2ab60336a0cca5.gif[/img]

Her projectile is a large ball of dark energy that leaves a trail of smaller energy balls. And each smaller projectile will target the closest opponent to surround them. A fantastic projectile that serves as both offense and defense, with the only caveat being that it costs quite a lot of your meter. Even if you fill your meter and unleash it, you won't be able to use it again for sometime as you collect more projectile orbs to get another chance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/f135bdce1c1272fd392dead30308d9313f912214.gif[/img]

Should you be cornered by a barrage of the opponent's projectiles, send them back by hitting the bomb button, which will transform every projectile into a bat that will attack the player. The bats aren't invincible and can be destroyed by the opponent's bullets, but with more of the opponents bullets means more projectiles they have to waste in order to get rid of the bats. But much like any other bullet type, the ball can also be used to destroyed them, so it's best to use her bomb when you have possession of the ball.

Her desperation is her legendary spear. Once the meter is filled, tap the desperation button to summon the spear. Use up and down to aim it and hit the projectile button to launch it at the opposing team. While almost all projectiles take 1 hitpoint, the spear can take away 3, nearly eliminating every character on a normal basis. Even if you miss hitting the opponent, the spear will crash on their wall, causing great damage, and the spear itself will explode into danmaku that can damage the opponent from behind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/ed80857373cf5e8d537383f6a201fa5bdd00b594.gif[/img]

And that does it for the characters in the current demo. Tune in next time as we delve into the rest of the roster for the upcoming second version of the demo.

notes.title: Introducing Reimu and Marisa
notes.notes:
In order to get you guys ready for the upcoming second demo where all characters will be available to play, I will be posting profiles for every character on the roster. Every announcement made will be showcasing two characters that have been paired into teams. Do note that these teams are not exclusive. You are free to edit the teams to whatever pair you wish, or even play with a single character only. These team were form for the story mode and it just became habit to reference the characters by the teams. That is why every character showcased will explain the character's abilities without referencing the other character so you may find it easier to see how one character can perform with any other in the roster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/6647cdc9b567044c2a6b08f4987746c01b23a0e5.png[/img]

[b]Pro[/b]: Well rounded character that leans on defense. Good for starters.
[b]Con[/b]: May be too basic for advance players.

Every game with a roster needs the well-balanced default character, and Reimu fits this bill. All her stats including movement, power, and meters are all aimed to be as equal and balanced as possible. But no character is perfect as Reimu seems to prefer to play it safe, so she leans more on defense rather than offense. Despite her preference for defense,  she can still hit the ball pretty hard and send it at a decent speed towards the opponent's wall. She is the perfect character for those learning how to play the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/e1ad9443a713163bc9fd6cc32ef35669a8e28a64.gif[/img]

Her projectile consists of 5 talismans that shoot out in an arc at a decent speed. This makes them easy to dodge so it is best to use as many as you can to keep the opponent on their toes. But be aware that her projectile meter isn't that big and you'll most likely fill it up in no time. A faster meter means not as much ammunition, but a filled meter can create a wall of talismans that will keep the opponent at bay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/d62b8bcd6aca46a954b70032e4e3a677139d24d4.gif[/img]

Her bomb is her reliable Fantasy Seal, where she emits great balls of light that eats up every projectile the opponent shoots. After lingering for a while, they will travel toward the opponent's field before dissipating. You do not have control over these orbs so it is recommended to use this as a defensive tool.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/79aba949f2d88d238efb9779432a54aaaba0c665.gif[/img]

Her desperation has her summon a large ying-yang orb that protects her. Any projectile within its radius gets eaten up. The orb remains as long as she has desperation in her meter which drains slowly, allowing the orb to remain around you for quite a bit of time, even longer if you continue to graze or collect the desperation power-up. But if you are willing to spend extra desperation, you can command the orb to be launched toward your opponent's side. The speed of the orb is quite fast so your opponent will have to act fast. And even if you they do manage to dodge it, the orb can still do 10 damage to their wall.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/d5ba53e03cff98fb54f83455433971af275092c9.png[/img]

[b]Pro[/b]: Fast meter-fill allows her access her projectile and desperation quickly.
[b]Con[/b]: Short bursts of magic makes her dependent on filling those meters.

Always ready for an adventure, Marisa is all about getting into the thick of it. Though her hitting power isn't too great, she makes it up for it with fast movements. But her real advantage is her magic. Really short meters allows her to build up her projectile and desperation quickly, but this comes at the cost of dispensing her magic as fast as she gets it. That is why she makes the most of it by utilizing quick bursts. It's all about getting to max as quickly as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/6aad24fc63a88af35296f7d21f469ddf680c3e0d.gif[/img]

Her projectile is a stream of stars that are shot in a spray pattern. The longer the linger, the bigger they get, forcing the opponent to think quickly. Her bomb is a quick flash of light that destroys any of the opponent's projectiles close to her, and after a while she summons two beams that will eat any additional projectiles. They extend enough to reach the opponent, but only linger for a short while before disappearing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/cf26a6f2ccca7afd4620835329ccc747267345d9.gif[/img]

But as everyone who is a fan of Marisa knows, her best well known attack is the ever favorite Master Spark, which is here as her desperation. And because people want to use it so much, her desperation is also a short meter. You might even gain the full desperation from a single volley of projectiles. But just as quickly you gain the go ahead to use it, so too does the beam disappear just as quick as it came. You can hold on to it for emergency cases, but there is a short time frame where the beam has to charge, leaving you open for attack. This is not meant as a replacement for the bomb as the opponent's projectiles can hit you while you are charging the attack. Holding it for emergencies is too risky because of that, and with the short time it takes to fill up the meter, it was meant to be used as often as possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45438903/79267f21d5d36abc8074b2b5d0bdc1d89fdf8cfc.gif[/img]

And this is just the start. We'll be going through the entire roster in the coming weeks, so stay tuned.

notes.title: Roster Reveal
notes.notes:
Ever since the release of the teaser demo last month, work has been diligently made to get to the second demo, and in turn, the finalized version of the game. I have been hard at work on the game, but as I've recently realized, hard work all the time isn't good for you. So that's why I took some time away from building the game to do some promo art, as well as write this announcement. I also wanted to just clear my mind to figure out what I'm going to do on the month of April.

But before I proceed to the topic, I want to take this moment to address the current teaser demo. I want to thank everyone who has tried the demo and given me feedback. I'll be making fixes and adding suggestions that you guys have provided during the development of the second demo. However, due to progress already being done, the teaser demo can't be updated anymore. So much of the code has been changed that it's practically impossible to make any changes at this point.

I'm also very aware of some players can't run the game. There's a bug that some players are experiencing where the game will crash during the loading screen. This doesn't seem to be happening to everyone, but it's hard to tell which players are experiencing this due to lack of information. So if you have experienced this crash, there is a thread on the Steam forums where you can post your specs. This information can help me determine what might be the cause. And even though I can't update the game, I can upload a beta build for testing purposes. There is a thread about the beta with instructions on how to access it. You can try running this beta, and if that doesn't give you result, then you can try booting the game from the exe file. Steam integration has been removed from that build so it should run.

Now let us proceed with how the game's been progressing. And throughout this time, it's been all about adding the rest of the roster. I'm happy to announce that all the planned characters are now in the game. They still need to be tweaked and tested but are pretty much playable. This announcement will serve as an introduction to each team that will be available upon the game's release along with a very brief description about how they will play.

notes.title: What to expect in the full release
notes.notes:
Development on the game continues. After the demo was released, no time was spared in its continuation. In fact, there's actually less time now than expected. This game has been in development for over a year but without much of a release date in the future and it all sounded like everything was on track. But life sometimes throws you a curveball, forcing you to change plans. In this case, the game will now be coming out this summer so there's no time to waste. However, at the moment, I am thinking of what my next move will be. I just finished a task that took me two weeks to complete and now I need time to think of what I'm going to be doing for the next few months. So I figured while I figure this out, I'll update you guys on what I am planning for the full release of the game.

But before we move on to the development of the game, I want to talk about the demo that I released two weeks ago. I can't believe that it's already been two weeks since the release of the demo because it feels like I spent an eternity to get to this point. And yet, even after a year of planning and development, one can't foresee all issues that may arise. It appears that people have experienced some bugs and mishaps that slipped in such as menus not working and controller issues. This is in part because of the time crunch I had and all that was done in a month.

But at least I am relieved that all these bugs were only in the menus because the gameplay was enjoyed by everyone. Aside from some adjustments that I made such as increasing the cost of Sakuya's projectiles, there didn't seem to be anything wrong with the gameplay, which makes me very happy to hear.

But this is only the beginning as this teaser does not truly represent what the final product will be. For as much as I spent an entire year to get to this point, it was mainly for the gameplay, setting up the rules, preparing the character template to include a bigger roster, items, game controller support, pretty much everything that happens after you select a character. Everything else outside of that, like the menus, was done in around a month before the release of the teaser demo. But now that I have the gameplay set, I feel like I can now concentrate more on the quality-of-life aspects of the game. So don't get too used to the teaser demo because everything is going to be overhauled to feel more polished. And these changes will apply to all aspects of the game including, but not limited to the following.

[strike]_________________________________________[/strike]

[h1]Characters[/h1]

This may be the least changed from the teaser demo as the characters you have played will pretty much function the same. Minor adjustments will be made so they may feel a bit different later one, but all the same, it should be no different. What will be different is that there will be a bigger roster, which I will reveal right now. With the addition of the four already playable, the game will include the following character teams:

-  Cirno and Daiyousei
- Youmu Konpaku and Alice Margatroid
- Aya Shameimaru and Nitori Kawashiro
- Yuugi Hoshiguma and Suika Ibuki
- Ran Yakumo and Chen

[h1]Controllers[/h1]

Controller support will be overhauled. The current controller support either has you using the keyboard or the gamepad. This has caused many issues, especially when editing button mapping. That is why the future release will do away with this and simply have you use both keyboard and gamepad. This will require an overhaul of the current controller setting so I won't be able to update the teaser demo for this. I apologize for this inconvenience but from here on, I will be putting consideration for both control types.

[h1]Better Interface Design[/h1]

Though it may not seem like much, something players simply take for granted, but part of quality-of-life improvements does include these little things. The font, the menu design, and even the sound effects. All these things are aspects I never really considered until after the demo was released. For example, the font used was something I never considered until I realized that I was going to translate this game into two languages. It was then that I realized that font that I chose for basic text was unsuitable for Spanish and Japanese. I will now be making plans to make the game easier to navigate and much more pleasant to look at to avoid the inconveniences that arouse in the demo.

[h1]Better Music[/h1]

I know some people didn't mind the background music, but I left that music as a final task and didn't have time to experiment with it. It was really just shoved out as fast as possible due to time constraints. I am very dissatisfied with how the music came out. Improving the music is now on my to-do list. 

[strike]_________________________________________[/strike]

There's plenty more to consider but these are just the bigger things I want to address. I want to thank all players who have played the game and provided both error reports and suggestions. I read all and make note of them. Though I'm sure by now you have played all that the teaser has to offer, but I still need more players to check it out. That is why I urge you that if you see the potential this game has, please share the game on social media and let others know about it. This game is planning to be bigger than what you see but I can't do it alone. All your help is greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

notes.title: What is the teaser demo?
notes.notes:
After a little over a year of development, I have finally released the first demo of the volleyball game, the teaser demo. But what is a teaser demo? It is a demo that showcases the fundamentals of the game rather while still representing what the final game could be like.

But another reason for this teaser demo is to get feedback before I go really deep into the game. If I offered a more robust demo, it may have been more difficult to make changes to it later on. The Teaser Demo is a smaller version of what I intend to offer in the final game. This way, if there are changes needed, I can do so relatively quickly as I build the game. That is why its very important to let me know what you think about the game on the Steam forums so that changes and improvements can be made.

What to expect from this Teaser Demo:

- Four characters available: Reimu, Marisa, Sakuya, and Remilia.
- A single demo of the main gameplay as well as a training room.
- Supports up to 4 human players.
- A preview of the partner AI system, where you can choose a set number of commands to your CPU partner.
- Keyboard and controller support, but gamepad is recommended.

So go ahead and download the demo and let me know what you think on the Steam forums.
